editorial:
Imagine moving into a quiet town where your new guardians seem nice but are hiding something dark. You play the role of the observer as a teenage girl tries to figure out why her adopted father and aunt are so terrified of a broken-down house in the woods. The vibe is very creepy and tense, making you feel like something bad is about to happen every time someone mentions the red house. It feels like a slow burn that builds up a lot of pressure, keeping you guessing about what exactly happened in that old building years ago.

The acting is solid, and the way the movie builds a sense of dread is great. While it moves a bit slow at times, the payoff is worth it. If you enjoy old-school mysteries that don't give away the answer too early, you will love this. Since it is an older film, you might want to track down a high-quality 4K Blu-ray for your physical collection to see the details clearly. If you are not a collector, renting it on Apple TV is a quick way to see if you like the style before committing to a full purchase.
endingExplained: You find out that the old man and his sister killed their own family members years ago to keep their money. They hid the bodies in the red house, which is why they kept the girl away from it. In the end, the truth comes out during a tense showdown. The bad guys cannot hide their crimes anymore, and the movie wraps up with the law finally catching up to them for their evil deeds.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves old mystery movies and family secrets.
